'''''Musango''''' is an [[extinct]] genus of [[unaysaurid]] [[sauropodomorph]] dinosaurs from the [[Upper Triassic]] ([[Norian]]) [[Pebbly Arkose Formation]] of Zimbabwe. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Musango matusadonaensis''''', known from a partial skeleton. ''Musango'' represents the fifth dinosaur genus to be named from Zimbabwe.<ref name=Musango>{{Cite journal|last1=Barrett |first1=P. M. |last2=Botha |first2=J. |last3=Sciscio |first3=L. |last4=Stuart |first4=B. P. |last5=Lovegrove |first5=J. |last6=Munyikwa |first6=D. |last7=Zondo |first7=M. |last8=Broderick |first8=T. N. |year=2026 |title=A new sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Pebbly Arkose Formation (Upper Triassic: Norian) of Kariba, Zimbabwe |journal= Journal of Systematic Palaeontology |volume=24 |issue=2 |article-number=2678610 |doi=10.1080/14772019.2026.2678610 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Discovery and naming ==

The ''Musango'' [[holotype]] specimen consists of five [[dorsal vertebra|dorsal]] (trunk) [[vertebrae]], at least two [[sacral vertebra|sacral]] (hip) vertebrae, at least 15 [[caudal vertebra|caudal]] vertebrae, [[dorsal rib]] fragments, [[gastralia]], three partial [[chevron (anatomy)|chevrons]], a left [[scapula]] and [[coracoid]] (shoulder blade), an incomplete left [[humerus]] (forearm bone), a manual [[ungual]] (hand claw), a partial left [[ilium (bone)|ilium]], a right [[pubis]] (hip bones), a partial right [[tibia]] and [[fibula]] (lower leg bones), the left [[astragalus (bone)|astragalus]] and [[calcaneum]] (ankle bones), a left [[metatarsal]], one pedal [[phalanx bone|phalanx]] (toe bones), and various indeterminate bone fragments. It was discovered in March 2018 on the margin of [[Lake Kariba]] by a South African/Zimbabwean-led expedition, and is permanently [[accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] in the [[Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe]] in [[Bulawayo]], Zimbabwe, under the code NHMZ 2583.<ref name=Musango />

In 2026, Paul Barrett and his colleagues [[species description|described]] NHMZ 2583 as belonging to a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaurs. The [[generic name (biology)|generic name]], ''Musango'', refers to the Musango Archosaur Site within the Musango Concession Area near the Musango Safari Camp on the shores of Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe, where the holotype was recovered. {{gloss|''Musango''}} is a [[chiShona]] word meaning {{gloss|living in the bush}}, which can be construed as a reference to the remoteness of the holotype locality. The [[specific name]], ''matusadonaensis'', refers to [[Matusadona National Park]], near the holotype locality.<ref name=Musango />

''Musango'' is the fifth genus of dinosaurs to be named from Zimbabwe,<ref name=Musango /> following [[Megapnosaurus|''"Syntarsus" rhodesiensis'']] in 1969,<ref name="raath69">{{cite journal |last1=Raath |first1=Michael A. |year=1969 |title=A new Coelurosaurian dinosaur from the Forest Sandstone of Rhodesia |journal=[[Arnoldia (journal)|Arnoldia]] |volume=4 |issue=28 |pages=1–25 }}</ref> ''[[Vulcanodon]]'' in 1972,<ref name="Vulcanodon">{{cite journal |last1=Raath |first1=Michael A. |year=1972 |title=Fossil vertebrate studies in Rhodesia: a new dinosaur (Reptilia, Saurischia) from near the Triassic-Jurassic boundary | journal=[[Arnoldia (journal)|Arnoldia]] |volume=5 |pages=1–2, 4}}</ref> and the contemporary ''[[Mbiresaurus]]'' in 2022<ref name="Mbiresaurus">{{Cite journal |last1=Griffin |first1=Christopher T. |last2=Wynd |first2=Brenen M. |last3=Munyikwa |first3=Darlington |last4=Broderick |first4=Tim J. |last5=Zondo |first5=Michel |last6=Tolan |first6=Stephen |last7=Langer |first7=Max C. |last8=Nesbitt |first8=Sterling J. |last9=Taruvinga |first9=Hazel R. |date=2022-08-31 |title=Africa's oldest dinosaurs reveal early suppression of dinosaur distribution |url= |journal=Nature |volume=609 |issue=7926 |pages=313–319 |language=en |doi=10.1038/s41586-022-05133-x |pmid=36045297 |bibcode=2022Natur.609..313G |s2cid=251977824 |issn=0028-0836}}</ref> and ''[[Musankwa]]'' in 2024.<ref name="Musankwa">{{Cite journal |last1=Barrett |first1=Paul M. |author-link1=Paul Barrett (palaeobiologist) |last2=Chapelle |first2=Kimberley E.J. |last3=Sciscio |first3=Lara |last4=Broderick |first4=Timothy J. |last5=Zondo |first5=Michel |last6=Munyikwa |first6=Darlington |last7=Choiniere |first7=Jonah N. |title=A new Late Triassic sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Mid-Zambezi Basin, Zimbabwe |journal=[[Acta Palaeontologica Polonica]] |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=227–241 |doi=10.4202/app.01100.2023|doi-access=free |hdl=10141/623186 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Description ==
Based on more complete relatives, ''Musango'' was likely an [[Bipedalism#Facultative and obligate bipedalism|obligate biped]]. A holotype individual's body length was calculated at about 4.5 meters and its body mass was calculated at about 222 kilograms.<ref name=Musango/>

== Classification ==
To determine the relationships of ''Musango'', Barrett et al. (2026) inserted it into the [[phylogenetic analysis]] of Barrett et al. (2024).<ref name=Musankwa /> This analysis placed ''Musango'' in the clade [[Unaysauridae]], as the sister taxon to ''Musankwa.'' A [[cladogram]] adapted from their analysis is shown below. Clade names have been inserted based on definitions from Otero & Peyre de Fabrègues (2022)<ref name=bookch2>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-95959-3_2 |chapter=Non-sauropodiform Plateosaurians: Milestones Through the "Prosauropod" Bauplan |title=South American Sauropodomorph Dinosaurs |series=Springer Earth System Sciences |date=2022 |last1=Otero |first1=Alejandro |last2=De Fabrègues |first2=Claire Peyre |pages=51–92 |isbn=978-3-030-95958-6 }}</ref> and Apaldetti & Martinez (2022)<ref name=bookch3>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-95959-3_3 |chapter=South American Non-Gravisaurian Sauropodiformes and the Early Trend Towards Gigantism |title=South American Sauropodomorph Dinosaurs |series=Springer Earth System Sciences |date=2022 |last1=Apaldetti |first1=Cecilia |last2=Martínez |first2=Ricardo N. |pages=93–130 |isbn=978-3-030-95958-6 }}</ref> for clarity.
